author: sara_teasdale

I have loved you so long, that now I know
You are only one of a number
Of things in which I like to take delight;
But not a thing more lovely than another.

And yet though such as these be all alike,
Yet each is dearer far than all before.
My heart has no control upon its will:
It takes with equal pleasure any hire.

In one particular city there’s no doubt of it
That he was born in a small house on the hill,
Where old walls rise up from ancient times to-day.

It may have been intended so at first; but there are other objects which cannot fail to engage the attention of American politicians sooner or later--objects which we must regard as more important than those of protecting an ally against a weaker foe. The most prominent among these are:

In the 1850s, a new movement was sweeping across America — the American Romantic Movement. At its core were three main principles: an emphasis on the individual; the primacy of emotion over reason; and a strong belief in intuition. While most Romantic artists were inspired by nature, two great landscape painters—Thomas Cole and Frederic Edwin Church—focused their attention on natural phenomena known as the sublime.

The word sublime is used to describe something that is beyond all bounds or limits, vastness itself. The awe-inspiring beauty and majesty of these scenes could only be described as sublime.
